comparisons.peer_topic: Commercial Paper Program Structure and Status
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company established a commercial paper program on November 3, 2022, allowing for unsecured notes up to $3 billion with maturities up to 397 days, but had no commercial paper outstanding as of December 28, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD maintain commercial paper programs structured as unsecured notes with maturities of up to 397 days and similar pricing mechanisms (discount from par or market-dictated interest rates). However, their program sizes and outstanding status differ: AVGO's program is capped at $2 billion, while AMD's is larger at $3 billion. As of their respective fiscal year-ends (November 3, 2024 for AVGO and December 28, 2024 for AMD), neither company had any commercial paper outstanding.

sentences.text: We have a commercial paper program pursuant to which we may issue unsecured commercial paper notes ("Commercial Paper") in principal amount of up to $2 billion outstanding at any time with maturities of up to 397 days from the date of issue.

Commercial Paper is sold under customary terms in the commercial paper market and may be issued at a discount from par or, alternatively, may be sold at par and bear interest at rates dictated by market conditions at the time of their issuance.
We had no Commercial Paper outstanding at either November 3, 2024 or October 29, 2023.

On November 3, 2022, the Company established a commercial paper program, under which the Company may issue unsecured commercial paper notes up to a maximum principal amount outstanding at any time of $3 billion with a maturity of up to 397 days from the date of issue.
The commercial paper will be sold at a discount from par or, alternatively, will be sold at par and bear interest at rates that will vary based on market conditions at the time of issuance.
During 2024 and 2023, the Company did not issue any commercial paper under the program and as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, the Company had no commercial paper outstanding.

comparisons.peer_topic: Commercial Paper Authorization and Outstanding Balance
comparisons.peer_summary: The company has Board authorization to borrow up to $10.0 billion under its commercial paper program, with no commercial paper outstanding as of both December 28, 2024, and December 30, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclosed that no commercial paper was outstanding at their respective fiscal year-ends. A key difference lies in the authorization caps: INTC has a much larger Board authorization of $10.0 billion, whereas AVGO's program is limited to $2 billion. Unlike AVGO's program which explicitly states it reduces revolving credit facility availability, INTC's disclosure focuses solely on the Board authorization and the zero outstanding balance without detailing interaction with other credit facilities in the cited sentences.
